La parte baja de la nube se carga negati: The lower part of the cloud becomes negative and the upper part, positive.
Dentro de una nube de tormenta hay corri: Inside a thundercloud there are very strong air currents that carry pieces of ice up and down. The small, light crystals are carried upwards; the soft, heavier hail falls.\n\nEach time they collide, the hail keeps electrons and the crystals lose them: it is the same triboelectric effect as when walking on a carpet. The result is a cloud with a positive top and a negative base. The exact details of the process are still being studied.
La nube y el suelo, un condensador gigan: The cloud and the ground, a giant capacitor
de capacidad entre la base de la nube y: of capacitance between the base of the cloud and the ground.
La base de la nube, con carga negativa,:
The base of the cloud, with negative charge, induces a positive charge in the ground below, just like the cable and the ground in a high-voltage line. Cloud and ground are two conductors separated by air: a capacitor.

As an order of magnitude, a base of $S = 10 "km"^2$ at $d = 2 "km"$ from the ground behaves like a parallel-plate capacitor:

$C = {ε_0 S}/{d} = {8.85 · 10^{−12} · 10^7}/{2000} ≈ 44 "nF"$

It is little capacitance, that of a small capacitor. What makes it dangerous is not that, but the voltage it is charged to.
Se carga hasta que el aire se rompe: It charges until the air breaks down
entre la nube y el suelo justo antes del: between the cloud and the ground just before the lightning.
Mientras la tormenta sigue separando car:
While the storm keeps separating charges, the voltage rises. With $V ≈ 100 "MV"$:

$Q = C V ≈ 44 "nF" · 100 "MV" ≈ 4.4 "C"$

The average field is $E = V/d = 50 "kV/m"$, far below the $3 "MV/m"$ that dry air withstands. But the field is not uniform: around the pockets of charge in the cloud and at the tips on the ground it is much greater, and there the air begins to ionise. Exactly how lightning starts inside the cloud is still a subject of research.
Un canal baja a saltos y el suelo respon: A channel descends in jumps and the ground responds
avanza el canal ionizado que baja de la: the ionised channel descending from the cloud advances, with pauses between jumps.
Desde la nube baja un canal de aire ioni: From the cloud descends a channel of ionised air, the stepped leader: it advances in jumps of a few tens of metres, with pauses of a few tens of microseconds, and branches. It is invisible to the naked eye.\n\nAs it nears the ground, the field at the tips of trees, rooftops and towers shoots up (the point effect, the same as St. Elmo's fire) and sparks rise from them towards it. When one meets the descending leader, the path is closed: cloud and ground joined by a thread of plasma.
de corriente de pico típica, durante una: of typical peak current, lasting a few tens of microseconds.
Al cerrarse el canal, el condensador se: When the channel closes, the capacitor discharges all at once: a wave of current rises from the ground towards the cloud at a third of the speed of light. That is the bright light of the lightning.\n\nThe charge that moves, $Q ≈ 4.4 "C"$, at a current of $I ≈ 30 "kA"$, takes about $Q/I ≈ 150 "µs"$. The air in the channel heats to about 30,000 K, five times the surface of the Sun. Several more strokes usually travel down the same channel, and that is why lightning flickers.
La energía que almacenaba el condensador: The energy stored in the capacitor was: $U = 1/2 Q V = 1/2 · 4.4 "C" · 100 "MV" ≈ 2.2 · 10^8 "J" ≈ 61 "kWh"$ A house uses that in about a week. But almost all of it goes into heat, light and a shock wave, and cannot be used: it is released in a fraction of a millisecond and in a place impossible to predict. The air in the channel, heated all at once, expands faster than the speed of sound and produces the thunder. The light arrives almost instantly; the sound takes about 3 s per kilometre. Count the seconds between the flash and the thunder to know how far away it struck.
los segundos entre el relámpago y el tru: the seconds between the flash and the thunder
